newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open mostly unchanged Friday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, dealers said.

Activity is expected to remain rangebound and thin ahead of a key USDA report due for release Monday at 0830 EDT. USDA will issue its first estimates of the new crop, along with the final estimates for the 1996/97 crop.
Analysts pegged the USDA's output estimate for 1997/98 cotton between 17.96 million and 18.80 million 480-lb bales.

Wet conditions continue to delay plantings across the U.S. cotton belt. Much of the crop in Texas is running behind schedule, while cool wet weather has delayed farmers in the Delta and the Southeast, Weather Services Corp, said.

Pakistan said output reached 8.742 million 375-lb bales as of Thursday, down from 9.944 million bales in the same year-ago period. Weak demand and high stocks are seen pressuring prices in Pakistan, dealers said.
Thursday, most-active July ended 0.20 cent higher at 72.12 cents a lb after trading from 72.45 to 71.85 cents. December finished 0.10 cent firmer to 74.56 cents.
Support remained at the contract low of 71.00 cents for July, followed by 70.00 cents.
NYCE said final delivery notices reached 770.
